metaTitle: Sliding Glass Door Repair Deerfield Beach | Condo Sliders
description: Sliding glass door repair in Deerfield Beach condos near the beach and inland: rollers, tracks, locks, Broward HVHZ rules and what the board decides.
h1: Sliding glass door repair in Deerfield Beach
subline: Beach condo balconies and inland condo buildings wear the same door parts at different speeds, and a new door answers to three sets of rules.
answer: Sliding glass door repair in Deerfield Beach usually means new rollers, a cleaned track and a readjusted latch, which leave the door's approval and look unchanged. A replacement is different. Broward County is in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, permits use the county's retrofit schedule, and your condo board's hurricane protection specifications apply.
closing: Send us a photo of both bottom corners of the moving panel and the track, and tell us whether the building is near the beach or inland. We'll tell you what we think is wrong.

faqs.q: Why does my Deerfield Beach slider take two hands to open?
faqs.a: Worn rollers or a dirty track, most of the time. When the wheels in the bottom rail wear flat or their bearings seize, they skid instead of rolling. Near the beach, salt corrodes steel bearings faster. Inland, years of dirt in the track do the same kind of damage more slowly.

faqs.q: Is a new sliding door in Deerfield Beach held to HVHZ rules?
faqs.a: Yes. Broward County is in the Florida Building Code's High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so a replacement door needs a product approval that covers HVHZ use, usually a Miami-Dade NOA or a Florida approval marked for HVHZ. Repairs to rollers, tracks and locks don't change the door's approval.

faqs.q: What is the Broward Uniform Retrofit Window & Door Schedule?
faqs.a: It's the shared form Broward's Board of Rules and Appeals requires for window and door replacement permits across the county. Each opening gets a line with its size, product approval, design pressure and glass type. Your contractor fills it out as part of the permit application for a new door.

faqs.q: Can my Deerfield Beach condo board reject the impact door I picked?
faqs.a: Not if it meets the board's adopted specifications. Under section 718.113(5) of the Florida Statutes, a board can't refuse hurricane protection that conforms to its specifications, but it can require the door to match the building's existing outside appearance. Get the specifications before you order.

faqs.q: Does the Deerfield Beach Community Appearance Board review door changes?
faqs.a: It can, for some buildings. The board reviews the exterior look of multi-family, commercial and industrial properties in the city. A repair that doesn't change how the door looks isn't an appearance change. For a new door in a different style or color, ask the city's planning staff first.
